parts.note: the writing implement draws its ink from a reservoir, a well, and its nib is a stylus or style for writing

explanation.surface: A question about whether some prose shows a good literary style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well-written' reads as praise of prose, but it describes ink drawn from a well inside the pen; 'style' is the old word for a writing point.
explanation.definitionFit: This writing implement holds its own ink supply, a reservoir that feeds the nib as you write.

definitions.meaning: suitability to take charge, as of a candidate fit to become a head
physical well-being, being in good shape

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both suitability for a post and the bodily condition of being in good shape.

parts.note: a fall from a horse at a riding school, which also leaves the rider distressed

explanation.surface: A rider falls off during a lesson at a riding school.
explanation.definitionFit: A fall or overturning, as when a rider comes off, and also the distress it causes.

clue.text: He has a heavy role at, reading, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters of at and reading are possibly rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor playing a weighty part at a read-through of the script.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At, reading' looks like a stage direction, but 'possibly' rearranges AT READING.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor who plays serious parts in plays of disaster and grief takes the heavy roles.

indicators.note: inconclusive means lacking its conclusion, so the final letter is cut off

parts.note: something perfect is ideal

explanation.surface: A notion that seems perfect but leads nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inconclusive' removes the last letter of IDEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion or concept that comes to mind is a thought.

parts.note: corporation is an old jokey word for a fat belly, and a Toby jug is shaped like a stout man with a large paunch

explanation.surface: A company that makes Toby jugs, the old pottery drinking mugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' looks like a company, but it is old slang for a big belly. A Toby jug is a traditional British mug shaped like a portly seated man.
explanation.definitionFit: A Toby jug's figure has a large rounded paunch, like a cooking pot.

indicators.note: about signals that the whole run of letters is turned round

parts.note: to moan is to complain

explanation.surface: A girl says she grumbles about things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' turns I MOAN round as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name, borne by Ruth's mother-in-law in the Bible.

clue.text: Does he treat one — who breaks down in the lab?…

definitions.text: Does he treat one — who breaks down in the lab?…

parts.words: Does he treat one — who breaks down in the lab?…
parts.note: a psychiatrist treats a patient who has broken down, and a laboratory chemist breaks substances down into their parts

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a doctor treats a patient who collapses at work in a laboratory.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue plays on two kinds of breaking down: a patient's breakdown, treated by a psychoanalyst, and a chemist breaking a sample down in the lab.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a psychoanalyst and a laboratory chemist examine things by taking them apart.

parts.note: in grammar the case showing possession, as in Latin, rather than a school case about property

explanation.surface: A dispute over ownership at a grammar school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grammar-school case' sounds like a school dispute, but it is a grammatical case: the one expressing possession.
explanation.definitionFit: In inflected languages such as Latin, this case marks ownership, like English 'of' or apostrophe s.

clue.text: Will cricket-match, by morning, have ten out?

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match
AM is the abbreviation for morning (ante meridiem)

indicators.note: out signals the letters of ten put out of their usual order

explanation.surface: A question about whether a cricket Test will see ten batsmen dismissed by morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' looks like the future-tense verb, but it is the noun, a legal document. 'Out' turns TEN into ENT. A Test is a full international cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: A last will and testament is the legal document setting out how a person's estate is to be left.

indicators.note: found in says the letters sit inside the run of words some garden

explanation.surface: Something final was discovered in a patch of garden.
explanation.definitionFit: The final letter of the Greek alphabet, hence anything that comes at the very end.

parts.note: in the Old Testament the Book of Job comes straight after the book named for this queen of Persia

explanation.surface: A question about who will take over a woman's job once she leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Job' looks like work, but it is the Book of Job, which follows the book of this queen in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: A biblical book about a Jewish queen of Persia, placed just before Job in the Old Testament order.

clue.text: Moving niftily with inner energy — showing Tom's quality

indicators.note: inner says the energy symbol goes inside the rearranged letters
moving signals that the letters of niftily are moved into a fresh order

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Something moving deftly and energetically shows the nature of a cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving' rearranges NIFTILY into FLINITY, and 'inner' puts E inside it after the F. A tom is a male cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A tom is a male cat, and this word names the nature of being catlike.

indicators.note: in an across clue on means placed after, so the downpour follows the street

parts.note: a downpour is heavy rain

explanation.surface: Heavy rain sweeps across a street, enough to block the view like a screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screen' looks like a noun for a barrier or display, but it is the verb meaning to sieve.
explanation.definitionFit: To screen material is to pass it through a sieve, which is also what straining does.

clue.text: Shopkeeper sought by victims of farmer's wife

definitions.meaning: someone who sells goods to the public

definitions.text: sought by victims of farmer's wife
definitions.meaning: in the nursery rhyme the three blind mice had their tails cut off by the farmer's wife, so they would want someone to put the tails back

explanation.walkthrough: In the rhyme 'Three Blind Mice' the farmer's wife cuts off their tails with a carving knife; the answer read as RE-TAILER restores them.
explanation.definitionFit: A seller of goods to the public, and also, as a coined word, one who would fit tails back on.

clue.text: Suit flat conversion in Galway, for example

indicators.note: conversion signals the letters of suit and flat converted into another order

explanation.surface: A suit gets adapted for a flat in the Irish city of Galway.
explanation.walkthrough: Galway looks like the Irish city, but it is Sir James Galway, the famous Northern Irish flute player.
explanation.definitionFit: James Galway is a celebrated flute virtuoso, so he is an example of a flute player.

parts.note: the post office impresses a stamp or mark on mail, so a letter without that impression has not been stamped

explanation.surface: Something untouched by the art movement Post-Impressionism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post-Impressionism' looks like the art movement, but it is the impression the Post Office stamps on a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Mail without a postage mark or stamp impressed on it has not been processed by the post.

indicators.note: in says the shortened poetry word is placed inside the letters of real
unfinished means the word for poetry lacks its final letter

parts.note: verse is poetry

explanation.surface: Unfinished poetry proves a real setback for a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfinished' cuts VERSE to VERS, which 'in' places inside REAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A reversal of fortune is a setback, a change for the worse.

clue.text: Dine out, embracing' nurse who is betrothed

indicators.note: embracing says the rearranged letters wrap round the word for nurse
out signals the letters of dine thrown out of their order

parts.note: to nurse someone is to tend them

explanation.surface: Someone engaged is going out to dinner and putting an arm round a nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' turns DINE into INDE, and 'embracing' places TEND inside it after IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's fiancé or fiancée is the one they mean to marry, their intended partner.

parts.note: evening here means making things even or smooth, as creases are smoothed out of clothes at home

explanation.surface: A former evening spent at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evening' looks like the time of day, but it is the verb 'evening', making smooth, as done to clothes at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing clothes with a hot appliance smooths out creases, a household chore.

indicators.note: away signals the letters of he's and far sent off into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A man has gone a long way off once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Away' rearranges the letters of HE'S FAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something anew means starting over, a second time.
A place much frequented, and a house said to be visited by a ghost.

clue.text: Smoking compartment used by John Jasper?

definitions.text: Smoking compartment used by John Jasper?

parts.words: Smoking compartment used by John Jasper?
parts.note: John Jasper in Dickens's The Mystery of Edwin Drood is an addict who frequents a den for smoking the drug from poppies

explanation.surface: A railway smoking carriage used by a man named John Jasper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smoking compartment' suggests a railway carriage; John Jasper is the drug-addicted choirmaster in Dickens's The Mystery of Edwin Drood.
explanation.definitionFit: A den was a place where addicts gathered to smoke the narcotic made from poppies.

indicators.note: about says the rearranged letters go around the time letter
possibly signals the letters of made are possibly rearranged

explanation.surface: A matchmaker's note: they made a pair, perhaps in time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' turns MADE into MAED, and 'about' puts it round T.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals that have been paired for breeding have been matched up.

clue.text: Sauna's out of order — the place is sub-tropical!

indicators.note: out of order signals the letters of sauna's put out of their proper order

explanation.surface: A sauna has broken down, which hardly matters in a warm climate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of order' looks like a broken sauna, but it rearranges the letters of SAUNA'S.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of the Bahamas sits in a warm sub-tropical climate.

definitions.meaning: a dark beer, of which this is a stronger kind

explanation.definitionFit: The word means sturdy or robust, and is also a strong dark beer like porter.

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A business's work enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen or cage for keeping hens is a small enclosure.

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Someone is awkward yet still finishes in record time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record time' looks like a fast finish, but 'record' is EP and 'time' is T.
explanation.definitionFit: An awkward, unskilful person is lacking in ability.

clue.text: Family taking wine in Greater Manchester

parts.note: stock means family lineage or descent
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: A family has some wine while in the Manchester area.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition names where the place is: STOCKPORT is a town in Greater Manchester, in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Stockport is a large town within the metropolitan county of Greater Manchester.

clue.text: Page in Iliad, perhaps, obsolete and in ruins

indicators.note: in says the page letter goes inside the rearranged epic
perhaps signals that Iliad is to be taken in some other order

parts.note: something obsolete is outdated

explanation.surface: A page of Homer's Iliad is so old and outdated it is falling apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' rearranges ILIAD into DILAI, and 'in' puts P inside it to make DILAPI.
explanation.definitionFit: A building fallen into disrepair and decay is in a ruined state.
